title: Revealing the gastric protective mechanism of Physochlaina physaloides (L) G. Don. with clinical orientation: PPAR/NF-kappaB signalling pathway activation.
authors: Li, Siqi; Feng, Wanze; Chen, Dongxue; Yu, Lan; Cui, Hongwei; Li, Minhui
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物对胃损伤的保护机制，涉及PPAR/NF-kB信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal diseases are global health issues. Current drugs for gastrointestinal diseases cause discomfort and toxicity; consequently, the use of traditional medicines and their extracts has gained attention in recent years. Physochlaina physaloides (L) G. Don. (P. physaloides) is traditionally used for diarrhoea and gastroenteritis; however, its material basis and mechanism of action for gastric injury have not been fully studied. PURPOSE: This study aims to explore P. physaloides and their protective effects on gastric injury, together with the potential mechanisms. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We constructed chronic gastritis and gastric ulcer models in rats using 56 % ethanol and anhydrous ethanol, respectively. Additionally, we screened gastric injury pathways via transcriptomics and the gene expression omnibus (GEO) database. Subsequently, we constructed an ethanol-stimulated GES-1 cell model and screened the active fraction of P. physaloides based on the cell survival rate and antioxidant activity. The effect of the active fraction of P. physaloides was investigated via tissue structure (HE staining), mucus secretion (PAS staining), anti-inflammatory activity, antioxidant activity, and gastric acid secretion levels. We employed liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to determine the active components of P. physaloides and the drug components in blood, before investigating the mechanisms via immunofluorescence, transcriptomic, metabolomics, network pharmacology, molecular docking, qRT-PCR, western blotting, and flow cytometry. RESULTS: The occurrence of gastritis, gastric ulcer, and gastric cancer is related to the PPAR/NF-kappaB signalling pathway, with decreased expression of FABP3 and PPARgamma, and increased expression of Bcl-2 and TNF-alpha. The n-butanol fraction of P. physaloides (BPP) showed significant improvement in cell survival and antioxidant activity in vitro. BPP also alleviated inflammation and oxidative stress in rat models, including by upregulating CAT, GSH, SOD, IL-10, PGE(2); downregulating VEGFA, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-alpha, and NO; improving pathological damage; restoring mucus levels; and reducing gastric acid secretion and macrophage expression. BPP and its active components, anisodamine and hyoscyamine, upregulated the expression of PPARalpha, PPARgamma, CPT1, and FABP3, and downregulated NF-kappaB p65, thereby regulating the PPAR/NF-kappaB signalling pathway for gastroprotection. The BPP and its active components did not significantly increase the expression of GPX4 and SLC7A11, nor did they reduce the production of ROS. Therefore, their effects are unrelated to ferroptosis. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence of the effectiveness of BPP in the prevention of gastric ulcers and treatment of chronic gastritis. We adopted a multidisciplinary approach to demonstrate that BPP and its active components, anisodamine and hyoscyamine, protect against ethanol-induced gastric injury by regulating the PPAR/NF-kappaB and non-ferroptotic cell death pathways. BPP and its active components can target PPARgamma and FABP3 and may have clinical application prospects to prevent gastric injury, which has unique advantages. These findings provide a scientific foundation for gastroprotection and expand the clinical applications of BPP.
abstract_zh: 背景：胃肠道疾病是全球性的健康问题。目前用于胃肠道疾病的药物会引起不适和毒性；因此，近年来传统药物及其提取物的使用受到关注。泡囊草（Physochlaina physaloides (L) G. Don.，P. physaloides）传统上用于治疗腹泻和胃肠炎；然而，其对胃损伤的物质基础和作用机制尚未得到充分研究。目的：本研究旨在探讨P. physaloides及其对胃损伤的保护作用，以及潜在机制。研究设计与方法：我们分别使用56%乙醇和无水乙醇构建大鼠慢性胃炎和胃溃疡模型。此外，我们通过转录组学和基因表达综合（GEO）数据库筛选胃损伤相关通路。随后，我们构建乙醇刺激的GES-1细胞模型，并根据细胞存活率和抗氧化活性筛选P. physaloides的活性部位。通过组织结构（HE染色）、黏液分泌（PAS染色）、抗炎活性、抗氧化活性和胃酸分泌水平，研究P. physaloides活性部位的作用。我们采用液相色谱-串联质谱（LC-MS/MS）测定P. physaloides的活性成分及血中药物成分，然后通过免疫荧光、转录组学、代谢组学、网络药理学、分子对接、qRT-PCR、western blotting和流式细胞术研究其机制。结果：胃炎、胃溃疡和胃癌的发生与PPAR/NF-kappaB信号通路相关，表现为FABP3和PPARgamma表达降低，Bcl-2和TNF-alpha表达升高。P. physaloides的正丁醇部位（BPP）在体外显著改善细胞存活率和抗氧化活性。BPP还减轻大鼠模型中的炎症和氧化应激，包括上调CAT、GSH、SOD、IL-10、PGE(2)；下调VEGFA、IL-6、IL-8、TNF-alpha和NO；改善病理损伤；恢复黏液水平；并减少胃酸分泌和巨噬细胞表达。BPP及其活性成分山莨菪碱（anisodamine）和莨菪碱（hyoscyamine）上调PPARalpha、PPARgamma、CPT1和FABP3的表达，并下调NF-kappaB p65，从而调节PPAR/NF-kappaB信号通路以实现胃保护作用。BPP及其活性成分未显著增加GPX4和SLC7A11的表达，也未减少ROS的产生。因此，其作用与铁死亡无关。结论：本研究首次提供BPP在预防胃溃疡和治疗慢性胃炎中有效性的证据。我们采用多学科方法证明，BPP及其活性成分山莨菪碱和莨菪碱通过调节PPAR/NF-kappaB和非铁死亡细胞死亡通路，保护乙醇诱导的胃损伤。BPP及其活性成分可靶向PPARgamma和FABP3，并可能具有预防胃损伤的临床应用前景，这具有独特优势。这些发现为胃保护提供了科学基础，并扩展了BPP的临床应用。
